Yes! You can generally bring a 20,000 mAh power bank on a flight in the United States, as long as it goes in your carry-on bag, not your checked luggage.

According to the FAA's battery travel rules, a typical 20,000 mAh lithium-ion power bank is well below the standard 100 watt-hour (Wh) limit.

What you need to know

Carry-on bag: Allowed

A typical 20,000 mAh power bank is about 72–74 Wh, below the 100 Wh limit.

Checked luggage: Not allowed

Spare lithium batteries and power banks must be kept in the aircraft cabin.

Airline-specific restrictions: Check first

Airlines may impose stricter limits on the number of power banks you can bring and whether you can use or recharge them during the flight.

Source: FAA — Airline Passengers and Batteries.

Tips before flying

Keep the power bank in your personal item or carry-on.

If your carry-on is gate-checked, remove the power bank and keep it with you in the cabin.

Protect it from damage and short circuits.

Check that its watt-hour rating is printed on the device or packaging, if possible.

Never fly with a damaged or recalled power bank.

Source: FAA — Lithium Batteries.

Bottom line: A standard 20,000 mAh power bank is generally fine to bring on your flight. Just keep it in your carry-on and check your airline's rules, particularly for in-flight use.
